name: Habits
problem: A small habit tracker for one person. I want to define a few daily habits, tick them off each day, and see streaks and a calendar of the last months. It runs locally in the browser and works offline.
aspects: Ticking a habit must take one tap and feel instant
Streaks must be correct across months, leap years and time zones
Data must never be lost when the page reloads
constraints: TypeScript, Vite, no UI framework heavier than Preact
Data stays in the browser (IndexedDB), no backend
Unit tests for the streak and calendar logic

outcome.summary_plain: You get a working habit tracker that runs in your browser with no server. You can add your own habits with a name and a colour, tick them off for today with one tap, and go back and fix any of the last seven days. Each habit shows its current and longest streak and a heatmap of the last six months. Everything is saved in the browser, so closing the tab or reloading keeps your data, and you can download it all as a JSON file and load it back later.

you_will_see.what: Today's date, a progress bar with 'x of N done', and one large row per habit: a coloured circle to tap, the name, a seven-day strip and the current and longest streak
The seven-day strip is tappable: each of the last seven days can be ticked or unticked straight from the row
A row of day chips for the last seven days (yesterday selected by default) and the habit list for whichever day you pick, so you can fix a missed day on the phone too
A six-month heatmap for the habit you select, with a missed/done legend
Working buttons: New habit, Reorder, Export JSON and Import
Set the name and pick a colour; rename, recolour or archive an existing habit (archived habits leave the list but keep their history)
Move habits up and down; the order sticks after a reload
Reloading the page keeps every habit and every tick; the app also opens with no internet connection after the first visit

stays_the_same: The look and the layout are the one you agreed on in sketch v1 (Today list): same dark theme, same colours, same row and card design, same order of the blocks down the page
Still one screen; the tab switcher used in the sketch to compare three directions is gone
The six-month heatmap stays a read-only picture — you cannot tick a day by clicking it there
Still local-only: no account, no sync, no backend, nothing leaves your browser
to_see_it: Run `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` and open the address it prints (http://localhost:5173)

open_questions.question: How far back should you be able to tick a day?
open_questions.proposed_answer: The last seven days, through the row strip and the catch-up day chips; older days stay visible in the heatmap but read-only
open_questions.why_it_matters: Editing arbitrary history means a date picker and tap targets on the nine-pixel heatmap cells, which is a different screen

open_questions.question: The sketch's catch-up block was fixed to 'Yesterday'. Turning it into a seven-day chooser adds a row of day chips above that card. Good?
open_questions.proposed_answer: Yes — same card in the same place, with a small row of day chips on top, yesterday selected by default; without it there is no way to fix a past day on a phone, where the seven-day strip is hidden
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the one visible addition to the agreed layout

open_questions.question: How do you pick which habit the bottom heatmap shows? In the sketch it was always the first one.
open_questions.proposed_answer: Tapping the habit's name selects it for the heatmap (the coloured circle stays a pure one-tap tick); the selected habit is remembered across reloads
open_questions.why_it_matters: The row has several tap targets, so the split has to be decided before the row is built

open_questions.question: When you import a JSON file, should it replace everything or merge with what is there?
open_questions.proposed_answer: Replace everything, after a confirmation dialog that says so
open_questions.why_it_matters: Merging needs conflict rules for habits with the same name, which is a lot more work

outcome.overview: Addressed: the brief does ask for past days, so rather than trimming the promise I extended `p1-today-screen` to actually build a full week of catch-up — the 7-day spark cells become tap targets on desktop, and the catch-up block gains a day-chip selector (defaulting to yesterday) so the same editing works at 375 px, where the spark is hidden. Acceptance criteria now check both paths, and the heatmap staying read-only is recorded as an open question.

scope.reason: A new single-screen browser app: persistence, one screen, habit management, export/import and unit tests. The owner already picked the layout in sketch v1, and there is no existing system or data to break.

process.why: Medium job (M, low risk): at most 3 phases, each reviewed.

handoff.summary_plain: The app now works exactly as scoped: you can add/rename/recolour/reorder/archive habits, tick today or any of the last 7 days with one tap, see correct current/longest streaks, and view a 6-month heatmap per habit. Everything is saved to IndexedDB (survives reload), and you can export/import your data as JSON. The app also now installs and works with no internet connection. The look matches the agreed sketch (dark theme, same cards/rows, tab switcher removed, heatmap stays read-only). The only nuance: on a phone-width screen the 7-day tick strip on each row is hidden by design — fixing a past day there goes through the 'Catch up' block instead, which is why that block exists as a 7-day chooser.

delivered.promise: Habits: create, rename, reorder, archive, name + colour
delivered.note: HabitDialog + reorder buttons + Archived panel, all wired to IndexedDB.

delivered.promise: Daily check-in: one tap today, editable for the last 7 days
delivered.note: Optimistic UI update, then async write; rollback on failure.

delivered.promise: Streaks: current and longest per habit
delivered.note: Heavily unit-tested across leap years, month/year boundaries, and DST in two time zones.
Heatmap cells are plain divs, not clickable, as agreed.

delivered.promise: Export to JSON / import back with replace-all confirmation
delivered.note: Import shows a confirm dialog stating it replaces all current data; malformed files are rejected with a clear message.
All state loads from IndexedDB on mount; selected habit for the heatmap also persists via localStorage.
vite-plugin-pwa generates a service worker + manifest; verified with a real offline browser reload in the task notes.

delivered.promise: Same look/layout as agreed sketch v1 (Today list), tab switcher removed, still one screen, still local-only
delivered.note: styles.css was copied byte-for-byte from the sketch; no `.switch` element remains.

delivered.promise: Seven-day strip tappable directly on each habit row
delivered.note: Works on desktop/tablet widths; CSS hides this strip on phone-width screens (≤560px), where only the Catch-up block below can fix a past day.

how_to_see: cd web && npm install (if not already done)
npm run dev — opens the app at the printed localhost URL (normally http://localhost:5173)
Tick a habit, reload the page, confirm the tick survived
Try New habit / Reorder / Export JSON / Import from the bottom bar
To check offline support specifically: npm run build && npm run preview, load the page once, then disconnect from the internet and reload — the app and your data should still appear
known_gaps: On phone-width screens the 7-day tick strip on each habit row is hidden by CSS; past-day edits there go through the Catch-up block instead (by design, but visually different from the desktop screenshot).
No 'new version available' prompt when the app updates itself offline — updates apply silently in the background (explicitly called out as in-scope-as-is in the build notes).
All automated checks (install, typecheck, tests, build) passed on their most recent runs — nothing is currently failing.
